- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >30% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in recognizing momentum; increase forecast slope gently to align with sentiment reversal.
- Model underestimates true volatility during high-sentiment periods; add 2–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underpredicts true price by 1–3% in early days of a new trend; apply slight upward bias in first 5–7 days of forecast window.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows without clear trend, model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 values before final output.
